items.example: What's your plan for the weekend?
items.simple: It is what you think you will do soon. You think first, then you do it.

items.en: I'm going to + verb: I'm going to visit my parents.
items.example: I'm going to visit my parents on Sunday.
items.exampleTr: Pazar günü annemle babamı ziyaret edeceğim.
items.simple: You already know what you will do. You say it with this.
items.note: Önceden karar verdiğin planlar için kullanılır.

items.example: Maybe we can meet on Saturday.
items.simple: It could happen, or it could not. You are not sure.

items.example: I'll probably stay at home tonight.
items.exampleTr: Bu akşam büyük ihtimalle evde kalacağım.
items.simple: It will most likely happen. It is almost sure.

items.en: I'll + verb: I'll call you later.
items.example: I'll call you later, okay?
items.simple: You say this when you choose something right now. It is a quick choice or a promise.
items.note: Anlık karar veya söz verirken 'will' kullanılır.

items.example: Are you free on Friday evening?
items.simple: You ask if someone has time on that day.
items.note: Bir şey önermeden önce sorulan çok doğal bir soru.

items.example: I'm not available on Monday.
items.simple: You have time and nothing else to do. You can come.

items.en: I'm thinking of + -ing: I'm thinking of moving.
items.example: I'm thinking of changing my job.
items.simple: You have an idea in your head about doing something. You are not sure yet.

items.example: We need to decide by tomorrow.
items.simple: You pick one thing from two or more things.

items.example: I haven't decided yet. I'll tell you tomorrow.
items.simple: You still do not know which one to pick.

items.example: I'll definitely come to your party.
items.simple: Yes, for sure. You have no question about it at all.

items.example: Can you arrange a meeting for Tuesday?
items.exampleTr: Salı için bir toplantı ayarlayabilir misin?
items.simple: You get things ready so they can happen. Like picking a day and a place.

items.en: What are you up to this weekend?
items.example: What are you up to this weekend?
items.simple: You ask what someone will do on Saturday and Sunday.
items.note: Gündelik konuşmada 'planın ne?' demenin rahat yolu.

items.en: I'm meeting + person: I'm meeting a friend tonight.
items.example: I'm meeting a friend for lunch tomorrow.
items.exampleTr: Yarın öğle yemeğinde bir arkadaşımla buluşuyorum.
items.simple: You say this when a friend and you are going to see each other. You already set the time.

items.example: I hope it doesn't rain on Saturday.
items.simple: You want something good to happen. You wish for it.

items.en: I might + verb: I might go out later.
items.example: I might go out later, but I'm not sure.
items.exampleTr: Belki sonra çıkarım ama emin değilim.
items.simple: It could happen, but you are not sure.
items.note: 'will'den daha belirsiz, yarı yarıya bir ihtimal.

items.example: My schedule is really full this week.
items.simple: This is a list of what you do and when. It tells you the time for each thing.

items.example: It depends on the weather.
items.simple: Sometimes one thing changes another thing. So you cannot say yes or no yet.

items.example: Let's postpone the trip until next month.
items.simple: You do something later, not now. You move it to another day.

items.example: I had to cancel our dinner plans.
items.exampleTr: Akşam yemeği planımızı iptal etmek zorunda kaldım.
items.simple: You say it will not happen anymore. You stop it.

items.example: I don't know yet. Let's see how it goes.
items.simple: You wait and look at what comes. Then you will know.

items.example: I'll let you know by tonight.
items.exampleTr: Bu akşama kadar sana haber veririm.
items.simple: You will tell someone later, when you know more.

items.example: What are your plans for the future?
items.simple: All the days that are still to come. Not today, not before.
